title: SMTP-DANE (RFC 7672): dedicated entry point, not a reuse of the HTTPS DANE path
description:
## Why

RFC 7672 SMTP-DANE has the strongest production deployment of any DANE flavour — MTAs negotiating TLS routinely use it for trust. A workspace that adopts DANE for HTTPS and not SMTP is incomplete. Replaces PKIX-j32w.6, which asked the question against a function (verify_smtp_signer) that does not exist and would have been the wrong home anyway: SMTP-DANE validates a mail SERVER's TLS certificate, not a signer.

## Why this cannot reuse verify_tls_server's DANE path

Three behavioural differences from HTTPS-DANE. The first makes a shared path wrong rather than merely incomplete.

### 1. Usage filtering — CONFIRM THIS FIRST

Current understanding is that RFC 7672 requires SMTP clients to ignore PKIX-TA(0) and PKIX-EE(1) records outright, because public CA trust is not meaningful between MTAs with no user to see a warning: only DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) apply.

THIS IS NOT CONFIRMED. Read RFC 7672 §3.1 and the surrounding text before writing any code. If it holds, then a shared code path with verify_tls_server would honour usage-0 and usage-1 records that SMTP-DANE requires be ignored — a silent policy violation, and the reason this needs its own entry point. If it does not hold, re-evaluate whether a shared path with a mode flag is adequate after all.

### 2. DNSSEC-validated MX lookup — reaches into the resolver

The TLSA owner name derives from an MX lookup, and that lookup must itself be DNSSEC-validated. An unvalidated MX lookup lets an attacker rewrite the MX record and point the connection at a server whose TLSA record they also control, which defeats the whole mechanism.

This is a pkix-dane-resolver requirement, not a wrapper concern: it needs a validated multi-step lookup (MX, then TLSA under the resulting hostname), with the DNSSEC status of BOTH steps surfaced. pkix-dane's TlsaResolver trait as shipped resolves a single TlsaName and has no MX concept. Expect either an additional trait method or a sibling trait in pkix-dane-resolver. Check whether this changes what PKIX-j32w.2 should build before that bead starts.

### 3. Reference identity

Which name the certificate must match follows RFC 7672's MX-derived rules rather than RFC 6125 hostname matching. Determine how this composes with pkix-identity rather than reimplementing name matching.

## Placement — open

PKIX-j32w.6 left this open: pkix-chain wrapper, or a sibling pkix-smtp crate. Decide once the resolver-side shape from difference 2 is known, since an MX-aware resolver trait may make a sibling crate the natural home.

## Also in scope

- RFC 7672's own opportunistic-vs-mandatory posture at the SMTP level, and how it composes with the DaneFailurePolicy decided in PKIX-j32w.4. These are different layers and may not agree; work out which wins.
- Whether the dane / dane-resolver feature split decided on PKIX-j32w.3 extends here unchanged.

## Depends on

pkix-dane 0.2.0 (shipped). Resolver work is PKIX-j32w.2; this bead should be read before that one starts, because difference 2 may widen its scope.

## Acceptance

[ ] RFC 7672 usage-filtering requirement confirmed against the RFC text and recorded
[ ] MX lookup is DNSSEC-validated, with the status of both lookup steps surfaced to the caller
[ ] Usage 0 and 1 records handled per the confirmed RFC requirement
[ ] Reference identity follows RFC 7672, composed with pkix-identity rather than reimplemented
[ ] Placement decided and recorded
notes:
PIECE A DONE 2026-11-24 (name checks). Pieces B (MX lookup) and C (entry point) remain, with the research they need recorded below.

## Done: RFC 7672 §3.2 name checks

- pkix_identity::verify_dns_name_with_cn_fallback -- §3.2.3 matching. 14 tests.
- pkix_dane::smtp behind a new `smtp` feature -- SmtpIdentities (the §3.2.2 set), SmtpNameCheck, SmtpNameError, verify_smtp_name. 18 tests.
- Five new pkix-identity fixtures for the CN-ID rule.
- Builds for thumbv7em-none-eabi with the smtp feature; 1990 workspace tests pass.

## Decisions made, with reasons

CN-ID: AN OPT-IN FUNCTION ON pkix-identity, not an SMTP-specific matcher.
RFC 7672 §3.2.3 requires CN fallback; pkix-identity refuses it for the Web PKI per RFC 6125 §6.4.4. Both are right for their protocol. Decided on pkix-identity because there must be exactly ONE wildcard implementation in the workspace -- a second would be a divergence hazard and wildcard bugs are security bugs. It is a separate function rather than a flag so no caller acquires CN fallback by default and the Web PKI path cannot be loosened by passing an argument. It delegates the DNS-ID path to verify_dns_name rather than reimplementing it.

Also note AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5: the workspace commits to standards-body specs. Declining to implement a standards-track IETF requirement anywhere would have been this workspace making policy.

PLACEMENT: a MODULE in pkix-dane behind a feature, not a sibling crate.
Same domain -- SMTP DANE is a profile of DANE -- and it keeps the crate count down while still giving a dedicated entry point, which is what this bead actually asked for. Splitting a module out later is easier than merging crates. The feature gate matters for a second reason: it keeps RFC 7672's CN-ID fallback out of an HTTPS-only consumer's dependency graph.

USAGE 0/1: treated as unusable, documented as TAKING THE MAY in §3.1.3 rather than as compliance. SmtpNameError::PkixUsageUnusable says so in its rustdoc.

## §3.2's MUST and DaneFailurePolicy -- still open, and sharper than filed

§3.2: "When at least one usable 'secure' TLSA record is found, the SMTP client MUST use TLSA records to authenticate the SMTP server. Messages MUST NOT be delivered via the SMTP server if authentication fails."

So RFC 7672 is opportunistic about WHETHER DANE is available and MANDATORY once a usable secure record exists. That is sharper than DaneFailurePolicy::Opportunistic, which permits falling back. The SMTP path must not offer a policy that allows delivery after a failed DANE authentication -- that is not a configuration choice, it is a MUST NOT. Needs reconciling in piece C, not merely composing.

## Research for piece B, the MX lookup -- READ THIS BEFORE DESIGNING IT

§2.2.1, MX resolution:
- TLSA records and the base domain are derived SEPARATELY FOR EACH MX hostname.
- MX records MUST be sorted by preference, AND: "an MX hostname with a worse (numerically higher) MX preference that has TLSA records MUST NOT preempt an MX hostname with a better (numerically lower) preference that has no TLSA records... prevention of delivery loops by obeying MX preferences MUST take precedence over channel security considerations." A naive "prefer the secure MX" implementation VIOLATES a MUST. This is the most surprising requirement in the document.
- CNAME expansion of the initial name, repeated to the MTA's recursion limit.
- Insecure MX RRset (or any CNAME leading to it) + DANE mandatory -> delivery MUST be delayed. Insecure + not mandatory -> free to use pre-DANE opportunistic TLS or cleartext.
- A client MAY still elect DANE TLS with an insecure MX RRset (the hosting-provider case: unsigned customer zone, signed provider zone with TLSA records). That is the case SmtpIdentities::insecure_mx exists for.
- SHOULD log unexpanded MX hostnames from insecure lookups, and "Any successful authentication via an insecurely determined MX host MUST NOT be misrepresented in the mail logs as secure delivery to the intended next-hop domain."
- No TLSA records, or only insecure ones -> DANE not applicable, proceed as pre-DANE opportunistic.
- "any errors during TLSA lookups MUST... cause the SMTP server in question to be treated as unreachable" -- downgrade protection.

§2.2.2, non-MX destinations -- AN ORDERING MUST THAT IS EASY TO MISS:
- "the SMTP client MUST perform any A and/or AAAA queries for the destination BEFORE attempting to locate the associated TLSA records."
- Why: load-balancing nameservers at some large providers mishandle TLSA queries, answering SERVFAIL or NOTIMP instead of an insecure negative reply, which would cause messages to be consistently delayed and ultimately returned to the sender.
- No address records -> unreachable. Address records found but the DNSSEC status of the FIRST query response is insecure -> SHOULD NOT look for TLSA records at all.

§2.1.1, security statuses:
- "indeterminate" is used exclusively in the RFC 4035 sense and "DNS records that would be classified 'indeterminate'... are simply classified as 'insecure'". "All 'insecure' RRsets MUST be handled identically."
- Consequence for us: pkix-dane's DnssecStatus has Secure/Insecure/Indeterminate/Bogus mapping hickory's Proof 1:1. The SMTP path MUST collapse Indeterminate into Insecure. That is a mapping in the SMTP code, not a change to the enum.

## Design note for piece B

The lookup POLICY is pure: which MX to try next, whether this RRset is secure enough, whether to issue a TLSA query at all, are all functions of DNS answers rather than of I/O. So piece B can be a sans-IO state machine in no_std pkix-dane -- the pattern already established by pkix_chain::sans_io -- with pkix-dane-resolver driving it and performing the lookups. That keeps AGENTS.md #1 and the Option C async placement, and makes the surprising MX-preference rule testable without a resolver.

## Not yet read

§2.1.2 (DNS error handling) and §2.1.3 (stub resolver considerations) in full, §6 (mandatory DANE, referenced by §2.2.1), and §8.1 (SNI support).

## Acceptance, revised

[x] RFC 7672 usage-filtering requirement confirmed against the RFC text and recorded -- it is undefined/MAY, not MUST
[x] CN-ID decided: opt-in function on pkix-identity
[x] Reference identifier set per §3.2.2, matching per §3.2.3
[x] Placement decided: a feature-gated module in pkix-dane
[x] §2.1 and §2.2 read before designing the MX lookup
[ ] Reconcile §3.2's MUST-authenticate-once-available with DaneFailurePolicy
[ ] MX lookup DNSSEC-validated, with the status of both steps surfaced, honouring the MX-preference MUST and the A/AAAA-before-TLSA MUST
[ ] The entry point that drives it
